Lower days can coexist with greater cash absorption
Q1 working-capital days improved from 37 to 32, while inventory days increased from 25 to 31. Debtor days stayed at
59; creditor days increased from 47 to 58. Management attributed part of the benefit to additional vendor credit in the
Middle East. Supplier support therefore explains more of the improvement than faster collections. [2, 3]
five extra funding days on FY28 base revenue of ₹166,000 crore tie up roughly ₹2,274 crore (sales

illustrative 25% tax rate. This is a sensitivity, not company guidance.
Q1 cash outflow is seasonal in part, but its similarity to the prior-year Q1 outflow does not remove the financing burden.

Valuation: growth needs to earn its
We value equity using shareholder-attributable earnings, with recurring Arena losses retained and exceptional gains
excluded. P/E avoids mixing parent earnings with a subsidiary enterprise-value numerator. A DCF would depend
heavily on working-capital assumptions that have not stabilized; a transparent earnings sensitivity is more useful here.
FY27 growth is below the Q1 rate as comparisons toughen and component-price effects fade. FY28 assumes
continued cloud/infrastructure expansion with modest margin improvement. The PAT-margin assumptions include
financing, tax, minority interests and a continuing Arena drag; they are a compact scenario model rather than a fully
integrated three-statement forecast. No dividend growth, acquisition benefit or exceptional gain is needed to reach the
14x is an analyst assumption balancing improving mix against thin margins, funding needs and
country risk. The 11x bear case reflects weaker growth and credit stress; 16x requires sustained profit growth and
credible cash conversion. These multiples are not presented as historical averages or peer-derived facts.
All E figures and scenarios are original estimates. Shares held constant at 78.1774 crore, corroborated by FY26 share capital and September
share-count reference [10]. Base value ₹416.17; modeled price upside 11.8%. An unchanged ₹6 future dividend would add about 1.6 percentage
points, but is not forecast or guaranteed. At the base EPS, a 1x P/E change moves value by about ₹29.73 per share. Consensus EPS, analyst count,
dispersion and broker targets were unavailable from a verified dataset.
